title: Invalid slope caliberation + connection at night + question
body:

Secondly, it is good, but has lot of bugs which really downs me from the app. 

Such bugs are being unable to caliberate. If i try to caliberate, it moves back right to the sugar without caliberation ( now cant show a pic since xdrip is closed, it is bugged for me for this sensor so when it ends ill be able to take a picture, but its a well known bug).

Other then that, the app is really awesome, please fix it soon, thanks.

@ben098765 : Which CGM and which xDrip-version are you using? Without this information we can hardly help you. Calibration should work fine - at least with Dexcom G6 on my side, using this CGM and a recent nightly xDrip+ build since 2 years.

About the "losing connection" issue - which Android version are you using? There have been issues with BT connections due to the Android update but this has been fixed with a recent nightly xDrip build. Check out the instructions by searching the github issues.

There are some messages you get from xDrip, if you are using a new G6, that can be confusing.  There are already open issues for that and they will be cleaned up hopefully soon.

There are some user behaviors that were fine with G5 but not with a new G6 that one should be aware of.  One example is frequent calibrations.  You shouldn't need to calibrate a G6 at all.  There is nothing wrong with testing your blood glucose with your meter.  But, calibrating every time you see a difference is not recommended.  

You should never calibrate a CGM if your trend is not flat or very close to flat.

If you restart a G6, using the original calibration code, you will interfere with factory calibration mechanism of G6. The result is that after the 2-hour warm-up, you will experience a significant error.  The readings will be much higher than they should be.
To calibrate, you need to limit the calibration to small values.  The recommendation is to limit the correction to 20% of the reading.  This means calibrating to a wrong value!  That is necessary to avoid a confused calibration error.  The result is that multiple calibrations will be required.   You should be able to get reasonably correct readings after 2 calibrations.  This could take up to one hour.

xDrip has issues and we are working on resolving them.  It may take a while.  In the meantime, we need to use the tool cautiously being aware of its limitations.
